# The shift mechanic is confirmed. Now I need to figure out the goal.
# Let me try clicking on a colored square to see if that does something different.
# I'll click on the top-left square at (19, 12) - currently S (sky blue)

action([{'action': 'MOUSE', 'row': 21, 'col': 14}])

# Check what changed
after3 = current_frame.segmentation['nodes']
sq3 = {}
for n in after3:
    if n['pixels'] == 16:
        b = n['boundary']
        min_r = min(p[0] for p in b)
        min_c = min(p[1] for p in b)
        sq3[(min_r, min_c)] = n['color']

frame_order = [
    (19,12), (19,18), (19,24), (19,30), (19,36), (19,42), (19,48),
    (25,48), (31,48), (37,48),
    (43,48), (43,42), (43,36), (43,30), (43,24), (43,18), (43,12),
    (37,12), (31,12), (25,12),
]

c2 = ['S', 'b', 'p', 'Y', 'g', 'p', 'b', 'S', 'g', 'p', 'S', 'b', 'b', 'w', 'w', 'g', 'p', 'S', 'w', 'g']
c3 = [sq3.get(pos, '?') for pos in frame_order]

print("After clicking colored square (21, 14):")
for i, (pos, a, b) in enumerate(zip(frame_order, c2, c3)):
    if a != b:
        print(f"  {i}: {pos}: {a} -> {b}")

# Check if red/green blocks changed
print("\nRed block:")
for n in after3:
    if n['color'] == 'R':
        print(f"  pixels={n['pixels']}, boundary={n['boundary']}")
print("\nGreen block:")
for n in after3:
    if n['color'] == 'N':
        print(f"  pixels={n['pixels']}, boundary={n['boundary']}")

print(f"\nBoard changed: {last_action_result.get('board_changed')}")
print(f"Gameplay changed: {last_action_result.get('gameplay_changed')}")
</parameter>
</function>
</tool_call>
